gloss: making a living; livelihood; scraping by

definitions.gloss: making a living; livelihood; scraping by
definitions.explanation: A literary term for earning just enough to survive. Literally 'pasting the mouth shut' — having just enough food to eat. Often implies a meager or modest existence.

examples.japanese: {翻訳|ほんやく}の{仕事|しごと}で{糊口|ここう}を{凌|しの}いでいる。
examples.english: I'm scraping by with translation work.

examples.japanese: {若|わか}いころは{日雇|ひやと}い{労働|ろうどう}で{糊口|ここう}を{凌|しの}いだ{時期|じき}もあった。
examples.english: When I was young, there were times I got by doing day labor.

notes:
USAGE:
Almost always used in the set phrase {糊口|ここう}を{凌|しの}ぐ (to eke out a living). A literary and somewhat old-fashioned expression. The character {糊|こ} means "paste" or "gruel," evoking the image of having barely enough thin porridge to feed oneself.

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- {糊口|ここう}を{凌|しの}ぐ (to eke out a living)
- {糊口|ここう}の{資|し} (means of livelihood)

SIMILAR WORDS:
- {生計|せいけい}: livelihood — a neutral, modern term for earning a living
- {食|く}いつなぐ: to keep oneself fed, to scrape by — a colloquial verb with a similar meaning
